newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, market seen recovering.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, market seen recovering.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mixed on Thursday with hoteliers rebounding and blue chip Pliva hitting an all-time-high and traders said the market was recovering.
"This is definitely a come-back of investors," Velimir Zelimorski of Fima brokerage told Reuters.
"We can expect prices to keep oscillating but not to the extent seen in the past weeks. The shares have now reached the bottom level and they are likely to either remain there or grow," he added.
Drugs firm Pliva, selling 284 shares, added 48 kuna to 13,700 -- the highest since being listed in April.
"This share is likely to keep its momentum, thanks to its strong research activity, especially in medications to combat diabetes," Zelimorski said.
Of 12 active issues five were up, six were down and one was unchanged.
Three hoteliers: Laguna, Suncani Hvar and Jadranturist were among the gainers.
Most actively traded hotelier was Suncani Hvar which sold 3,644 shares, closing 10 kuna up at 70, while the top gainer Laguna added 100 kuna to 1,200 per share on a small volume of 39 units.
"These stocks are the favourites as they proved their quality by remaining relatively stable throughout the turbulences of the market", he said.
Blue chip Zagrebacka Banka was the most actively traded issue with 3,655 units sold, sliding down 5 kuna to 1,015.
Among the active issues was also Podravka which sold 3,068 shares, closing two kuna down to 235.
Turnover dropped to 9.1 million from 13.4 million, while volume was up at 13,190 shares from 11,606.
